description: (0.5.0) Bucket watch filters (RFC-ACDP-0018 §6.1): lineage_bucket and agent_bucket match by a prefix of SHA-256 over the watched value, so the registry learns a bucket, not the value. Registry scenarios A–F are behavioral and apply when the registry advertises limits.max_change_bucket_length; consumer scenarios G–I are behavioral; the bucket-derivation vectors are executed by scripts/conformance-runner.py.

input.setup: Producer P publishes X (lineage Lx) and Y (lineage Ly), where the first hex digit of SHA-256(Lx) equals that of SHA-256(Ly) and their 4-digit prefixes differ. X and Y are both retracted. P's key is revoked by R (controller P). An unrelated producer Q's context V (lineage Lv, in a different 1-digit bucket from Lx) is retracted.

scenarios.name: A — lineage bucket returns the whole bucket

expected.behavior: lineage_bucket=<first hex digit of SHA-256(Lx)> returns the retractions of both X and Y (same bucket), and not V's. The registry MUST NOT narrow the result to any single lineage: every visible entry whose lineage_id hashes into the bucket is returned.
lineage_bucket=<first 4 hex digits of SHA-256(Lx)> returns X's retraction and not Y's.

scenarios.name: C — agent bucket hears revocations by controller

expected.behavior: agent_bucket=<first 4 hex digits of SHA-256(P)> returns X's and Y's retractions and R's key_revocation entry (its agent_id is the controller P, §4).

Bucket values are OR'd with each other and with ctx_id, lineage_id and agent_id; kind is AND'd with the result. lineage_bucket=<bucket of Lv>&agent_bucket=<bucket of P>&kind=key_revocation returns R's entry only. Each bucket value counts once toward max_change_filters: a request whose ctx_id, lineage_id, agent_id, kind, lineage_bucket and agent_bucket values total more than max_change_filters is schema_violation (400).
Each of these is schema_violation (400): an empty value; a value with an upper-case hex digit; a value with a non-hex character; a value longer than max_change_bucket_length (here 9 digits).

scenarios.name: F — cursors and visibility are unchanged

expected.behavior: A bucket-filtered page follows every §5 rule: ascending seq, next_cursor always present, an empty page with has_more: true when the bucket matches nothing in the scanned range, and visibility no wider than retrieval (§5.5). A restricted entry in the bucket stays hidden from a requester who may not retrieve it.
The consumer computes each bucket as the first n lowercase hex digits of SHA-256 over the UTF-8 bytes of the lineage_id or agent_id exactly as it appears in entries, per the vectors below.

Given scenario A's response, a consumer watching only Lx processes X's retraction and ignores Y's: a bucket response is a candidate set, and the consumer applies its own exact match before §7 verification. It MUST NOT treat Y's entry as concerning anything it relies on.

scenarios.name: I — no buckets without the limit (consumer)

expected.behavior: A registry's capabilities omit limits.max_change_bucket_length. The consumer sends no lineage_bucket or agent_bucket parameter to it: it polls unfiltered, or with exact filters if it accepts revealing them. It never sends a bucket longer than the advertised maximum.

vectors.name: bucket-lineage-001
vectors._note: The input is the whole lineage_id string, prefix included. Hashing only the 64-hex digest after 'lin:sha256:' gives not_bucket_4, which is wrong.

vectors.name: bucket-agent-did-web-port
vectors._note: The DID string exactly as it appears in the entry, percent-encoding included. Decoding %3A to ':' first gives not_bucket_4, which is wrong.
